title: Open-Weight Model Adoption Gate
summary: Review model identity, license, provenance, artifacts, runtime, evaluation, security, operations, and rollback before adopting an open-weight model.
prerequisites: An identified model repository and immutable revision
A target runtime and hardware profile
Security, legal, data, and operational owners

sections.title: Verify what is being adopted
paragraphs: Open weight is not the same as open source, unrestricted use, safe serialization, reproducible training, or vendor support. Record publisher, repository, immutable revision, base and derivative lineage, license and acceptable-use terms, model card, intended uses, limitations, training and evaluation disclosures, file formats, hashes, runtime, and required remote code.

Prefer safer serialization formats where supported, inspect dependencies and custom code, isolate initial loading, scan artifacts, and prevent an unreviewed repository update from replacing the approved model.

A Hugging Face model card is a README.md containing Markdown and metadata about intended uses and limitations, training information, datasets, and evaluation results. Relationship metadata can identify a base model or a derivative such as an adapter, merge, quantized model, or finetune. This metadata supports discovery, but it is not independent proof of publisher identity, authenticity, safety, legal clearance, or deployment approval. See https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/model-cards.

The Hugging Face model release checklist at https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/model-release-checklist is a source-specific publishing procedure. Following or claiming to follow that procedure does not by itself prove that a particular artifact is authentic, safe, legally cleared, or approved for deployment.

Worked synthetic case A, recorded evidence: Fictional Atlas-7B-Instruct names publisher Fictional Atlas Research, repository fictional://atlas/atlas-7b-instruct, immutable derivative revision 4f8c2a1, base model Fictional Atlas-7B revision 91aa0d7, transformation instruction-finetune-job-ft-44, artifact atlas-int8.bin, and claimed SHA-256 aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa. Provenance record ATLAS-PROVENANCE-001 states: 'FICTIONAL EVIDENCE: The publisher record names base revision 91aa0d7, derivative revision 4f8c2a1, transformation instruction-finetune-job-ft-44, and artifact atlas-int8.bin.' This passes the record-completeness check for identity and lineage, but the fictional publisher and digest have not been independently authenticated.

Atlas terms record LR-118 states: 'FICTIONAL EVIDENCE: Reviewer J. Rivera recorded that a license file and acceptable-use notice were located; scope and distribution questions remain assigned to the authorized legal owner.' This supplies an exact review record but is not a legal conclusion. Atlas runtime manifest BM-44 states: 'FICTIONAL EVIDENCE: Runtime Fictional Runtime 1.4.2, tokenizer tok-22, int8 conversion conv-08, custom code disabled, and hardware profile one fictional 24 GB accelerator.' These fields identify the build to inspect without claiming that the runtime is safe.

Atlas evaluation record EV-77 states: 'FICTIONAL EVIDENCE: Evaluation binds derivative revision 4f8c2a1, base revision 91aa0d7, tokenizer tok-22, int8 conversion conv-08, Fictional Runtime 1.4.2, and hardware profile one fictional 24 GB accelerator. The record contains populated sections for quality, refusal, prompt injection, privacy, timeout, crash recovery, and load testing.' No benchmark values or actual execution are claimed. Operations record OP-12 names patch, abuse, capacity, rollback, and incident owners, records rollback target revision 2e1d901, and expires the evidence on 2026-11-18.

Atlas traceable decision on the frozen review date 2026-09-19: identity, lineage, runtime, quantization, hardware, evaluation binding, ownership, and unexpired-record checks pass for the supplied fictional records. Terms remain with the authorized legal owner. Artifact integrity remains conditional on an independently calculated digest matching a trusted manifest held outside the candidate record. The outcome is RECORD_CHECK_PASS only after that toy record check succeeds. It is not publisher authentication, legal clearance, safe-runtime verification, production verification, or deployment approval.

Worked synthetic case B, blocking evidence: Fictional Cedar-13B-Chat names candidate revision 77c91fe and q4 quantization. CEDAR-PROVENANCE-101 states: 'FICTIONAL EVIDENCE: Model card says derived from Cedar-13B but gives no base revision, transformation record, or parent digest.' CEDAR-ARTIFACT-102 states: 'FICTIONAL EVIDENCE: Trusted intake manifest expects cedar-q4.bin SHA-256 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111; the candidate record claims 2222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222.' Missing lineage and the changed artifact each independently require REVIEW_REQUIRED.

Additional Cedar stops are concrete. CEDAR-CODE-103 states: 'FICTIONAL EVIDENCE: Repository loader requests custom code; review pending.' CEDAR-EVAL-104 states: 'FICTIONAL EVIDENCE: EV-19 covers revision 12ab000, fp16, and a different runtime, while the candidate is revision 77c91fe and q4.' CEDAR-EXPIRY-105 states: 'FICTIONAL EVIDENCE: Approval evidence expired 2026-08-01.' Against the frozen date 2026-09-19, custom code is unreviewed, evaluation is bound to a different build, and evidence is expired. Any one blocks the record check. Preserve the records, quarantine the candidate, establish lineage independently, review code without executing it in production, evaluate the exact build, and obtain renewed authorized decisions.

sections.title: Gate quality, security, and operational readiness
paragraphs: Evaluate the exact quantization, runtime, prompt format, safety controls, and hardware build that will be deployed. Test normal, boundary, adversarial, privacy, tool-use, load, timeout, crash, and recovery cases; a base-model benchmark does not validate a derivative deployment.
Assign owners for patch and model monitoring, vulnerability response, abuse handling, scaling, capacity, cost, backup, rollback, license change, and end-of-life.

Keep authority separated. Research findings identify what sources support and where evidence is unavailable. Writer findings explain how the case maps evidence to a decision. Verifier findings check shapes, hashes, bindings, dates, and expected outcomes. Adversary findings attempt to bypass the gate with changed artifacts, incomplete lineage, unreviewed code, mismatched evaluations, expired evidence, malformed records, or self-asserted approvals. None of these roles may silently convert RECORD_CHECK_PASS into deployment approval.

Research finding: the cited Hugging Face documentation supports the description of model cards and relationship metadata, while also leaving authenticity and safety to independent evidence. The release checklist is provider-specific. The retained OpenAI gpt-oss-20b URL is evidence about that model page only, and its page contents were not reverified for this repair. No supplied source establishes a universal open-weight adoption standard.

Writer finding: the Atlas and Cedar cases are explicitly fictional and include evidence excerpts rather than evidence identifiers alone. They bind decisions to exact revisions, lineage, runtime, quantization, hardware, evaluation, review records, and expiry. Verifier finding: the offline program uses a frozen date, strict record shape, a fixed harmless filename, a trusted manifest outside the candidate JSON, and assertions for every expected result. Adversary finding: matching metadata, matching hashes, or all claimed booleans cannot establish publisher trust, a license conclusion, safe execution, or deployment authorization.

Provider-neutral transfer: apply the same evidence questions separately to MetaLlama, DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, Phi, NVIDIANemotron, Z.ai, gpt-oss, and other model families. Collect each model's own repository, immutable revision, lineage, terms, runtime, hardware, and exact-build evaluation records. This list makes no universal claim about any family's license, capability, quality, safety, or support.

Changed-input task, complete this before reading the answer key: start with the supplied passing candidate record and change exactly one item. Choose a digest, base revision, custom-code review state, evaluation binding, or expiry date. Record the changed field, affected evidence, expected result, and stop or recovery action. Do not treat claimedApproved, model-card metadata, or a self-reported matching digest as authority.

Answer key: changing the candidate digest or altering the local fixture produces REVIEW_REQUIRED because the calculated digest no longer agrees with the trusted manifest. Remove baseRevision and the result is REVIEW_REQUIRED because lineage is incomplete. Set customCodeRequired to true and customCodeReviewed to false and the result is REVIEW_REQUIRED because code review is unresolved. Bind evaluationRevision, evaluationRuntime, evaluationQuantization, evaluationHardware, or evaluationBaseRevision to another build and the result is REVIEW_REQUIRED. Set decisionExpires to 2026-09-18 and the result is REVIEW_REQUIRED because it precedes the frozen date 2026-09-19. In every case, stop the toy record flow, preserve evidence, and obtain corrected independent evidence. Do not download or execute a model as part of this exercise.

Evaluation: [EXACT BUILD -> QUALITY, SAFETY, SECURITY, LOAD, AND COST]
Stop conditions: [UNKNOWN LINEAGE, UNACCEPTABLE TERMS, UNSAFE CODE, OR CRITICAL FAILURE]
Verification: [ISOLATED LOAD, REPRODUCIBLE BUILD, END-TO-END GATE, AND MONITORING]
Recovery: [DISABLE ROUTE, RESTORE VERIFIED ARTIFACT, REVOKE ACCESS, AND RECONCILE DATA]

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes immutable provenance, hashes, terms review, model card, artifact and dependency scan, exact runtime and hardware manifest, evaluation results, deployment controls, owners, monitoring, fallback, and decision expiry. Verify a clean isolated load and reproducible deployment before production data is available.

Stop when lineage, license, artifact integrity, custom code, required safety performance, or operating ownership is unresolved. Recover by disabling the route, revoking model access, preserving hashes and logs, restoring the last verified artifact and configuration, reconciling affected data, and retesting the complete gate.

Model-card metadata, matching hashes, and claimed approval booleans never establish publisher trust, legal clearance, safe runtime, or deployment approval. The exercise below reports only RECORD_CHECK_PASS or REVIEW_REQUIRED. All actual deployment remains outside this toy exercise pending authorized independent verification. It does not download a model, execute model code, run a benchmark, verify production controls, or reach a license conclusion.

Exercise files are check_gate.py, harmless-fixture.txt, and candidate_record.json. In a new empty directory, save the supplied Python as check_gate.py. Run python3 check_gate.py --write-fixtures to create the two deterministic harmless fixtures. Inspect them, then run python3 check_gate.py. Only Python 3 standard-library modules are used. The program accepts no candidate path, rejects an unexpected artifact filename before file input, and reads only the fixed local fixture and candidate names.

Expected output is exactly these status lines in this order: candidate: RECORD_CHECK_PASS; pass: RECORD_CHECK_PASS; digest_mismatch: REVIEW_REQUIRED; changed_artifact: REVIEW_REQUIRED; missing_lineage: REVIEW_REQUIRED; custom_code_unreviewed: REVIEW_REQUIRED; evaluation_binding_mismatch: REVIEW_REQUIRED; expired_evidence: REVIEW_REQUIRED; malformed_shape: REVIEW_REQUIRED; missing_field: REVIEW_REQUIRED; malformed_json: REVIEW_REQUIRED; missing_file: REVIEW_REQUIRED; unexpected_filename: REVIEW_REQUIRED; all_true_claims_cannot_override_failure: REVIEW_REQUIRED. The semicolons here separate output lines. The script itself prints one result per line.

The assertions execute every listed negative case and cause a nonzero exit if an observed result differs from its expected result. The changed_artifact test actually changes the harmless local bytes and restores them in a finally block. Missing file and malformed JSON are controlled failures. The trusted manifest is held in the program rather than accepted from candidate_record.json, and it binds the artifact to the expected publisher, repository, revision, base lineage, transformation, runtime, quantization, hardware, and evaluation identifier.

After inspection, delete check_gate.py, harmless-fixture.txt, and candidate_record.json. Do not replace the harmless fixture with a downloaded model, point the program at arbitrary paths, or execute repository-provided code. No execution is claimed here; the output is the expected result of running the supplied program and fixtures as instructed.
